subject: music
topicDisplay: Area Of Study 6 Contemporary Traditional Music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In African music, the 'master drummer' typically...?
options: Leads the ensemble, signalling changes and improvising over the cyclic patterns
Sets up the instruments before the performance
questions.explain: The master drummer leads, cues changes and improvises over the underlying cyclic patterns.

questions.q: In ensemble performance, good 'ensemble skills' include all of the following EXCEPT...?
options: Watching for cues and breathing together
Maintaining a shared sense of pulse
Listening and balancing dynamics with other players
Deliberately ignoring the other performers' tempo
questions.explain: Strong ensemble playing depends on listening, balancing and keeping together, not ignoring fellow performers.

questions.q: In the alap–jhor–jhalla–gat structure, the 'gat' section is distinguished by...?
options: A return to the unmetred opening
A solo drone with no melody
The entry of the tabla and a fixed, composed melody with a regular tala
questions.explain: The gat is the composed, metred section where the tabla enters and a fixed melody is set within a tala.

questions.q: Gamelan ensembles commonly use which two tuning systems?
questions.explain: Gamelan typically uses the five-note slendro and the seven-note pelog tuning systems.

questions.q: A 'drone' as a textural device (e.g. in Indian or Celtic music) is...?
options: A sustained note or notes held continuously beneath the melody
questions.explain: A drone is a continuously sustained pitch (or pitches) underpinning the melody.

questions.q: Gamelan music frequently uses 'interlocking' (kotekan) parts, meaning...?
options: Two parts combine, each playing alternate notes, to create a single faster composite line
The ensemble plays in strict Western major scales
All players double the same melody an octave apart
questions.explain: Interlocking parts dovetail, each playing alternate notes so that together they form one rapid composite line.

questions.q: In the typical structure of a North Indian raga performance, the opening section is the 'alap', which is characterised by...?
options: A fast, fixed composition with drumming
A slow, free, unmetred exploration of the raga without tabla
questions.explain: The alap is the slow, unmetred opening that introduces the raga's notes, performed without the tabla.

questions.q: In Indian classical music, a 'raga' is best defined as...?
options: A fixed rhythmic cycle of beats
A melodic framework of notes and characteristic phrases used as the basis for improvisation
The drone instrument that sustains the tonic
questions.explain: A raga is the melodic framework, comprising a set of notes and characteristic phrases, on which improvisation is built.

questions.q: The compositional device of 'augmentation' refers to...?
options: Lengthening the note values of a theme, usually doubling them
Raising the pitch of a theme
questions.explain: Augmentation lengthens a theme's note values, typically doubling each duration.

questions.q: In an Indian classical ensemble, which pairing of instruments is most typical?
questions.explain: The sitar plays the melody while the tabla provides the rhythmic accompaniment.

questions.q: In African drumming traditions, the West African 'djembe' is...?
options: A set of tuned metal gongs
questions.explain: The djembe is a goblet-shaped West African hand drum capable of a wide range of tones.

questions.q: A 'cyclic' or 'ostinato' pattern, common in African drumming, is...?
options: A pattern that constantly changes and never repeats
A short rhythmic or melodic pattern repeated continuously as a foundation
questions.explain: Cyclic patterns repeat a short rhythmic or melodic cell continuously, forming the music's foundation.

questions.q: In composition, developing a musical idea through 'sequence' means...?
options: Repeating a melodic pattern at a higher or lower pitch
questions.explain: A sequence repeats a melodic or harmonic pattern at a different pitch level.

questions.q: When 'arranging' an existing melody for a new ensemble, a composer is chiefly concerned with...?
options: Transposing it down exactly one semitone only
Re-scoring and adapting existing material for different forces while retaining its essence
Inventing an entirely new melody unrelated to the original
questions.explain: Arranging adapts and re-scores existing material for different forces while preserving its identity.

questions.q: The 'tabla' is...?
options: A pair of hand drums of different sizes and pitches
questions.explain: The tabla is a pair of tuned hand drums central to North Indian rhythmic accompaniment.

questions.q: The Indonesian 'gamelan' is primarily an ensemble of...?
questions.explain: A gamelan is built chiefly from tuned metallophones, gongs and drums.

questions.q: The Argentine 'tango' is most associated with which instrument providing its characteristic sound?
questions.explain: The bandoneón, a button accordion, gives the tango its distinctive timbre.

questions.q: In the context of performance, 'idiomatic writing' for an instrument means...?
options: Writing that ignores the instrument's natural strengths
Writing only in the treble clef
Writing that suits the technique, range and characteristic capabilities of the instrument
questions.explain: Idiomatic writing exploits the natural technique, range and strengths of the specific instrument.

questions.q: In Celtic folk music, a 'jig' is most commonly in which metre?
questions.explain: The jig is a lively dance typically in compound 6/8 time.

questions.q: In Indian classical music, the 'tala' refers to...?
options: The melodic ornamentation of the soloist
The cyclic rhythmic framework, a repeating cycle of beats
questions.explain: Tala is the rhythmic cycle, a repeating pattern of beats that organises the music in time.

questions.q: The 'jhalla', the closing section of a North Indian raga performance, is characterised by...?
options: Silence with only the drone sounding
A fast, exciting climax with rapid rhythmic strumming
A return to the opening alap
A slow, free and unmetred mood
questions.explain: The jhalla is the fast, rhythmically exciting climax that ends the performance.

questions.q: A 'reel', another Celtic dance type, is usually in...?
options: Simple quadruple time (4/4 or cut common) with a flowing quaver movement
questions.explain: The reel is a fast dance in simple quadruple time with continuous even quavers.

questions.q: The Latin American 'clave' is best described as...?
options: A characteristic two-bar rhythmic pattern underpinning many Afro-Cuban styles
questions.explain: The clave is a foundational two-bar rhythmic pattern that organises much Afro-Cuban and Latin music.

questions.q: 'Call and response' is a texture common in African (and African-American) music in which...?
options: The music has no fixed pulse
Two unrelated melodies are played simultaneously
A leader's phrase (call) is answered by a group (response)
All voices sing exactly the same line throughout
questions.explain: In call and response a soloist's call is answered by the group's response, an antiphonal texture.

questions.q: The continuous sustained background pitch in Indian classical music, often provided by the tanpura, is called the...?
questions.explain: The drone is the sustained pitch (usually tonic and dominant) supplied by the tanpura beneath the melody.

questions.q: In Indian classical music the term 'bol' refers to...?
options: Mnemonic syllables used to represent and recite drum strokes or rhythms
questions.explain: Bols are spoken mnemonic syllables representing tabla strokes and rhythmic patterns.

questions.q: In performance, 'interpretation' refers to...?
options: Transposing the music to a new key
The performer's expressive choices of dynamics, phrasing, tempo and articulation within the score
Playing the notes exactly as printed with no expressive choices
questions.explain: Interpretation is the performer's expressive shaping of dynamics, phrasing, tempo and articulation.

questions.q: In fusion music, an artist such as Ravi Shankar collaborating with Western musicians most exemplifies...?
options: The blending of Indian classical techniques (raga, tala, sitar) with Western elements
questions.explain: Such collaborations blend Indian classical features like raga, tala and sitar with Western musical elements.

questions.q: In sub-Saharan African music, 'polyrhythm' refers to...?
options: The simultaneous combination of two or more contrasting rhythms
The use of only one drum
A single rhythm played in unison by all performers
A gradual slowing of the pulse
questions.explain: Polyrhythm layers two or more contrasting rhythms sounding at once, a defining feature of much African music.

questions.q: 'Fusion' music is best defined as...?
options: A style that blends elements of two or more distinct traditions or genres
Music performed only on acoustic instruments
questions.explain: Fusion combines features of two or more traditions or genres, such as jazz-rock or Indian-Western fusion.
